mcqs.q: An impression tray is a device used to:
opts: Carry, confine and control the impression material while making an impression
Pour and store the final cast
mcqs.explain: The tray carries, confines and controls the impression material in the mouth.

mcqs.q: The three parts of an impression tray are the:
mcqs.explain: Tray parts: handle, flange and body.

mcqs.q: A water-cooled rim-lock tray is specifically used for which impression material?
mcqs.explain: Water-cooled rim-lock trays are for agar; non-water-cooled rim-lock trays are for alginate/RBIM.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a recommended method of sterilizing impression trays?
mcqs.explain: Trays are sterilized by autoclave, dry heat or chemical vapor; disposable trays are recommended.

mcqs.q: The five objectives of an impression are preservation, support, stability, esthetics and:
mcqs.explain: The objectives (P-S-S-E-R) are preservation, support, stability, esthetics and retention.

mcqs.q: Maximum coverage of the denture-bearing area provides the 'snowshoe effect', which mainly improves:
mcqs.explain: Broad coverage spreads occlusal load over the tissues (snowshoe effect), aiding support (and thereby stability, retention and preservation). By distributing forces over the widest area.

mcqs.q: Excess pressure during the impression technique is undesirable because it leads to:
mcqs.explain: Pressure recorded in the impression becomes denture pressure, damaging soft tissue and resorbing bone (poor preservation).

mcqs.q: Denture stability decreases with:
opts: Loss of vertical ridge height or an increase in flabby, movable tissue
mcqs.explain: Stability depends on close adaptation to firm mucosa; it falls as ridges resorb or flabby tissue increases.

mcqs.q: 'Adhesion' as a retention factor is the physical attraction of:
opts: Unlike molecules (saliva to the mucosa and the denture)
Like molecules within the saliva layer
mcqs.explain: Adhesion = attraction of unlike molecules (saliva–mucosa and saliva–denture); cohesion = attraction of like molecules within the saliva layer.

mcqs.q: For atmospheric pressure to aid denture retention, the denture must have:
opts: A perfect (effective) seal around its entire border
mcqs.explain: Atmospheric pressure resists dislodging forces only if there is a complete peripheral border seal.

mcqs.q: Which materials are commonly used for PRELIMINARY impressions?
mcqs.explain: Preliminary impressions use impression compound, alginate, or putty-consistency elastomers. Silicone.

mcqs.q: Dental plaster (β-hemihydrate) and dental stone (α-hemihydrate) differ mainly in:
opts: Particle form/porosity, giving stone greater strength
Their chemical formula (one is not gypsum)
mcqs.explain: Both are calcium sulfate hemihydrate; α-hemihydrate (stone) has denser, less porous particles and is stronger than β (plaster).

mcqs.q: When mixing gypsum for a cast, you should:
opts: Add the powder to the water and spatulate 30–60 s, then vibrate to remove bubbles
Add water to a fully mixed powder
mcqs.explain: Add powder to measured water, spatulate 30–60 s and vibrate to reduce bubbles.

mcqs.q: The base of a poured cast should have a minimum thickness of about:
mcqs.explain: A cast base should be at least ~15–16 mm thick at its thinnest point for strength.

mcqs.q: The cast should be separated from the impression:
opts: About one hour after the initial set
mcqs.explain: Separate the cast about one hour after the initial set, then trim and finish.

mcqs.q: At the first patient visit, which laboratory procedure runs in parallel with taking the preliminary impression?
opts: Pouring the preliminary cast, then making the wax spacer and custom tray
Mounting the casts on an articulator
mcqs.explain: Selecting the stock tray and taking the case history are the other clinical steps of visit 1.

mcqs.q: Metallic impression trays are made of:
mcqs.explain: Non-metallic trays are plastic and acrylic resin trays.

mcqs.q: Stock trays are supplied in which forms?
mcqs.explain: A custom (special) tray, by contrast, is made individually for the patient on the preliminary cast.

mcqs.q: A NON-perforated tray achieves retention of the impression material by:
mcqs.explain: Perforated trays give mechanical retention through the holes.

mcqs.q: A NON-water-cooled rim-lock tray is used for:
mcqs.explain: The water-cooled rim-lock tray is the one specific to agar.

mcqs.q: A preliminary impression is defined as a negative likeness made for the purpose of:
opts: Diagnosis, treatment planning, or the fabrication of a tray
mcqs.explain: The cast poured from it — the preliminary cast — serves the same three purposes.

mcqs.q: Excess pressure during the impression technique matters because:
opts: Pressure in the impression becomes pressure in the denture, damaging soft tissue and bone
Pressure in the impression improves the peripheral seal
Pressure in the impression shortens the setting time
Pressure in the impression has no effect on the finished denture
mcqs.explain: This is why preservation of the residual ridge is the first objective.

mcqs.q: Regarding the ESTHETICS objective, the vestibule should be:
opts: Filled, but not overfilled, to restore facial contour
Left unfilled to allow muscle movement
Filled only in the anterior region
mcqs.explain: Border thickness is varied with each patient's needs, matching the extent of the residual ridge, and provides lip support.

mcqs.q: 'Cohesion' as a factor in denture retention is the physical attraction of:
opts: Like molecules — acting within the saliva layer between the denture base and mucosa
Unlike molecules — saliva to the mucosa and to the denture
The denture base to the residual ridge
mcqs.explain: Adhesion is the attraction of UNLIKE molecules.

mcqs.q: Which undercuts are described as extremely helpful to retention?
opts: The lateral tuberosities, maxillary premolar, distolingual and lingual premolar areas
The incisive papilla and the midpalatine raphe only
The hamular notches and the vibrating line only
The genial tubercles and the masseteric notch only
mcqs.explain: Mechanical locking into undercuts is one of the five retention factors.

mcqs.q: Muscular control as a retention factor is described as:
mcqs.explain: Patient tolerance explains why some function without complaint despite ill-fitting or even broken dentures.

mcqs.q: Which gypsum product is the stronger, and what is it called?
mcqs.explain: Beta hemihydrate is dental plaster; alpha hemihydrate is dental stone.

mcqs.q: When mixing gypsum for a cast, the water is added first in order to:
opts: Slowly wet the powder and remove trapped bubbles
mcqs.explain: The mix is spatulated for 30–60 seconds in a rubber bowl, then vibrated to reduce bubbles.

mcqs.q: When pouring a cast, the mix should be:
opts: Allowed to run in from one end while the impression is held on the vibrator
Poured into the centre of the palate first
Packed in with a spatula without vibration
mcqs.explain: The material is flowed all around with light vibration; the extra material forms the base.

mcqs.q: Powder for a gypsum mix is ideally dispensed by:
opts: Weighing it on a scale, with the water measured in a graduated cylinder
Using a manufacturer's scoop without weighing
mcqs.explain: Accurate proportioning is what makes the cast dimensionally reliable.

saqs.q: Define an impression tray and list its parts and four ways of classifying trays.
saqs.a: An IMPRESSION TRAY is a device used to carry, confine and control impression material while making an impression. PARTS — handle, flange and body. CLASSIFICATIONS — by material (metallic / non-metallic), extent (stock — full-arch, sectional or quadrant — or custom), dentition (edentulous / dentulous), and retention or design (perforated / non-perforated / rim-lock).

ans.text: A device used to carry, confine and control impression material while making an impression.

saqs.q: State the five objectives of an impression and briefly explain support.
saqs.a: The five objectives are PRESERVATION, SUPPORT, STABILITY, ESTHETICS and RETENTION. SUPPORT is provided by MAXIMUM COVERAGE of the denture-bearing area, giving the SNOWSHOE EFFECT that distributes applied forces over as wide an area as possible — which in turn helps preservation, stability and retention.

ans.text: SUPPORT is provided by maximum coverage of the denture-bearing area, giving the snowshoe effect — distributing applied forces over as wide an area as possible. This in turn helps preservation, stability and retention.

saqs.q: List the five factors affecting denture retention.
saqs.a: 1) ADHESION — attraction of unlike molecules; saliva to mucosa and to the denture. 2) COHESION — attraction of like molecules within the saliva layer. 3) MECHANICAL LOCKING into undercuts — lateral tuberosities, maxillary premolar, distolingual and lingual mandibular premolar areas. 4) ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE — needs a perfect peripheral seal. 5) MUSCLE CONTROL and patient tolerance — a largely learned process.

head: Factor
Mechanism
rows: attraction of unlike molecules — saliva to mucosa and saliva to the denture
attraction of like molecules within the saliva layer
into undercuts — lateral tuberosities, maxillary premolar, distolingual and lingual mandibular premolar areas

saqs.q: Name the materials used for preliminary casts and describe how a cast is poured.
saqs.a: Preliminary casts are poured in β-HEMIHYDRATE (dental plaster) or α-HEMIHYDRATE (dental stone). Weigh the powder and measure the water; add powder to water and spatulate 30–60 s, then vibrate out bubbles. Dry excess water from the impression, hold it on a vibrator and let the mix flow from ONE END around the impression, fill it, and form the base (≥ 15–16 mm) from the extra material — the inversion method. Separate about one hour after the initial set, then trim and finish.

steps: Add powder to water and spatulate 30–60 s, then vibrate to remove bubbles
Hold it on a vibrator and let the mix flow in from one end, all around the impression
Fill the impression and form the base (≥ 15–16 mm) from the extra material — the inversion method
Separate about one hour after the initial set, then trim and finish

saqs.q: How should impression trays be prepared before use, and which three materials are used for preliminary impressions?
saqs.a: PREPARATION — trays should be cleaned properly and STERILIZED before use; DISPOSABLE trays are recommended; sterilization is by AUTOCLAVING, DRY HEAT or CHEMICAL VAPOURS. MATERIALS FOR PRELIMINARY IMPRESSIONS — (1) impression compound, (2) irreversible hydrocolloid (alginate), and (3) elastomers in PUTTY consistency, that is addition or condensation silicone.

list: Trays should be cleaned properly and sterilized before use
Sterilization is by autoclaving, dry heat or chemical vapours

head: Material
rows: Elastomers in putty consistency — addition or condensation silicone

saqs.q: List the ways impression trays are classified, with an example of each.
saqs.a: 1) MATERIAL — metallic (stainless steel, aluminium) or non-metallic (plastic, acrylic resin). 2) MANUFACTURE — stock trays, pre-made as full-arch, sectional or quadrant, or custom (special) trays made individually on the preliminary cast. 3) DENTITION — edentulous (no teeth) or dentulous (with teeth). 4) RETENTION — perforated, whose holes retain the material mechanically, or non-perforated, needing an adhesive. 5) RIM-LOCK — a beading that retains materials not adhering to the tray; water-cooled for agar, non-water-cooled for alginate.

head: Classified by
Types and examples
rows: metallic — stainless steel, aluminium · non-metallic — plastic, acrylic resin
stock trays, pre-made as full-arch, sectional or quadrant · custom (special) trays, made individually for the patient on the preliminary cast
perforated — the holes give mechanical retention · non-perforated — needs an adhesive
a beading retaining materials that do not adhere to the tray — water-cooled for agar, non-water-cooled for alginate

saqs.q: Describe how a cast is poured by the inversion method, and the requirements for the base.
saqs.a: Dry the excess water from the impression. Hold it on the vibrator and let the mix run in from ONE END, flowing the material all around with light vibration and filling the impression sufficiently; the extra material forms the base. The base needs a MINIMUM THICKNESS OF 15–16 mm at its thinnest portion. Separate the cast about ONE HOUR after the initial set, then trim and finish — the diagnostic casts are then ready for diagnosis, treatment planning and custom-tray fabrication.

steps: Dry the excess water from the impression
Hold it on the vibrator and let the mix run in from ONE end, flowing it all around with light vibration
Fill the impression — the extra material forms the base
Separate about one hour after the initial set, then trim and finish

ans.text: The base needs a minimum thickness of 15–16 mm at its thinnest portion. The casts are then ready for diagnosis, treatment planning and custom-tray fabrication.
